chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: Is the proposal for bandwidth for explicit only or any form of Canfidate path.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: As currently described it is for bandwidth reservation for specific explicit paths.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: At least that is my read.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: This is not true that bandwidth management was not in the early view. The view was that SR is a stateless fabric. Distrinuted orchestration method  are part of the SR solution since Day1. These drafts brings RSVP-TE states in the SR network. Is this is OK, that is a question for the Spring WG and another draft on agenda asks that question.

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: i am assuming there is no BGP/PCEP here there are no controller...

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: As far as I know ther eis no PCEP (or BGP) ask here.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: Path compute for RSVP-TE can be done at PCE.

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: Would be good to understand what is the operational reality when controller is a no-go for that operator

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: and also what benefits they saw for going to SR but want to bring in RSVP - i.e why go hybrid, if the existing RSVP-TE already does it all. What was the motivation for going to SR and now porting this in?

chat.author: Shraddha Hegde
chat.text: @Zafar This is providing distributed bandwidth management without any controller and the network nodes themselves doing bandwidth management. RSVP state are only in control plane not in fwding plane

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: Martin, I locked the queue for time.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: What does it mean to say "RSVP state in the forwarding plane"?

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Forwarding plane has LFIB

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: LFIB exists in MPLS-SR

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Some people prefer the SR data plane.  This adds bandwidth management.

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text:
I'll put my comment here: I don't agree that "sophistic dated bandwidth management" requires either RSVP like resource reservation (and state!), or a central controller.
I think it can also be done sophistically by just centrally verifying and - if needed - tuning the distributed routing (i.e. IGP). No need for realtime controllers.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Knowledge about bandwidth utilization needs to be somewhere.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Your choice is centralized or decentralized.

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: also +1 to Andrew: this does requires state everywhere, and IIRC the main purpose of SR was to get rid of it.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: It requires control plane state, no additional data plane state.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: I agree with Martin.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: SR sacrificed bandwidth management in doing so.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: isn't the main driver for SR was also control plane state explosion and data plane was a side effect? i.e RSVP refreshes being troublesome? (was before my time ...)

chat.author: Nat Kao
chat.text:
+1 to Martin.
Not sure it's the right direction.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: RSVP refreshes were a protocol and implementation issue.  Fixed long ago.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: The problem has been solved without RSVP-TE states.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Not without a controller.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: There should be a review of all approaches by the Spring WG

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: @Tony: in practice this knowledge does not have be realtime. In fact, getting your possible failure cases right, e.g. including actual SRLG, is - for some (including me) - more valuable than realtime state keeping in mid nodes.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Bandwidth management is inherently a realtime operation.  The demand matrix is a function of time.

chat.author: Rakesh Gandhi
chat.text: @Tarek, If this is meant for only using adjacency SIDs, does it mean that it is for circuit-style SR policy use-case?

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Tony is right that previous to this work, doing b/w reservation in SR required a central controller. This introduces an approach using a distributed control plane

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: The authors assumed RSVP-TE is the only distributed way. This is where discussion should first need to go.

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: @Tony: While this might matter in theory, it does not for all operators, as they might have pretty regular periodic loads and overlaid by long term trend.

chat.author: Adrian Farrel
chat.text: Oh, Zafar, what other distributed b/w reservation mechanisms exist?

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: Nothing applies to ALL operators.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: There are MANY operators who have bandwidth management requirements.  They actively use RSVP-TE today. Something like 85% of Internet backbone traffic flows through an existing RSVP-TE network today.

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: @Tony: I was merely  saying that the mentioned modes are not the only sophisticated ones. The presentation claimed that.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: Happy to doc as an info draft

chat.author: Martin Horneffer
chat.text: "Something like 85% of Internet backbone traffic flows through an existing RSVP-TE network today."  I do know countries for which this is not correct.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: @Martin: If you have an oracle, of course.  However, I'm fresh out.

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: I also do not believe 85% claim is correct.

chat.author: Tarek Saad
chat.text:
Hi Rakesh,
Strict-paths SR paths are only a subset of SR paths - for operators that want to leverage the value on non-strict paths (node SID ECMP and path redudancy) - this solution (as is) can not do reservation on such paths

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: Tarek the natural progression is RSVP-TE signalled SRv6 MPTE  (in the queue...)

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: I agree with what Jie saud. There are many gaps in the drafts. It would be good to evaluate all the gaps in a holistic manner. There is a holistic doc later in the agenda, that would be a good place to start the conversation.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: +1 for Zafar. The bandwidth coexistence raised one, i suspect there's other thorns that will appear

chat.author: Tarek Saad
chat.text: @Andrew Stone, I was hoping for similar answer (future work, etc.), but Pavan sounded as if we don't want to solve this usecase

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: It is also not clear if RSVP-TE facility backup protection for protected Adj SID or RSVP-TE LSP can be protected with TI-LFA (in a backward compitable manner)

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: Some networks use RSVP-TE mainly for local protection, would be good if more information on networks using RSVP-TE for bandwidth reservation could be provided

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: For SR-MPLS, I do not see any gain. Why not Just use RSVP-TE using local labels. No breaking of dark bandwidth, per hop label accounting, deployed ... etc.

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: Could you please share a specific list of outstanding gaps on the mailing list? My understanding is that we have addressed all the questions and concerns raised during the MPLS WG adoption poll. If there are additional issues that still require a response, it would be helpful to have them explicitly identified so we can address them. It is difficult to make progress on concerns that have not yet been articulated.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: @Zafar Ali  So, you're saying that SR has no benefits?

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: For @liusong there was no specific action for the draft. It's how do we choose to do SR use cases for S-BFD. When doing it, please discuss implications when candidate paths can be encoded multiple ways and what each use case means.

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: For networks which do need bandwidth reservation, it needs to be clear what kind of reservation they are expecting

chat.author: Zafar Ali
chat.text: The draft in MPLS WG for RSVP-TE signaling in SR-MPLS network does not bring any value. In fact it is inferior to the what is deployed today.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @joel unless the "sbfd" has a use case presented and approved by spring - we cannot judge the requirements for BGP.   Pce adoption of BFD shows interest, but we need a firm use case to judge the parameters in SBFD.  ....

chat.author: Tarek Saad
chat.text: @Pavan, my concern is  we are pushing a solution that will not allow restrict an SR operator from using non-strict SR paths. It sounds as if a trade-off needs to be made between TE and specific SR paths

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: This is an expansion of Jeff's comment.

chat.author: Joel Halpern
chat.text: @susan Hares Understood.

chat.author: Tony Li
chat.text: I concur, but there are many customers who insist on using SR.

chat.author: Jim Guichard
chat.text: folks, respectfully, there are many interwoven questions/comments, that imho would be better served by  documenting them through the mailing lists.

chat.author: Dhruv Dhody
chat.text: Also, PCEP BFD extension is not SR specific

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: SBFD is widely used for SR Policy

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @Jim .. was that a comment to me or RSVP?

chat.author: Jim Guichard
chat.text: RSVP

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Tarek -- I don't see any issue with using only Adjacency SIDs for bandwidth-reserved TE Paths -- this is because the reservations are made per traversed TE link; If the concern is the length of the segment-list -- this is addressed by delegation

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: And we use BGP SR Policy to deliver the path to the headend node from the controller.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: SBFD is used to check the liveness of the SR policy path.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: So that the backup path can take over when the active cp goes down

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: All good use cases for S-BFD.

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Yes. In SR Policy production networks, S-BFD is MUST not optional.@Jeff @Joel

chat.author: Tarek Saad
chat.text:
@Pavan, an operator may be already deploying SR-paths over non-strict path. If they are interested in reserving BW (e.g. using RSVP), you are telling them modify your SR-path to become strict. This may not be desirable. 
I'll give another well-known example in SR which is NULL-endoint - Again, this solution will restrict ability to steering and reserver BW over such paths

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: Zhenqiang... we just need spring to agree tht your use cases are valid to start bgp work

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Understood.

chat.author: Susan Hares
chat.text: @zhenqiang .... mail list agreement ia fine.  Joel is reading this and he can help

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: @Pavan / @Shraddha - i haven't thought through it enough but is this going to require a change in definition to the SR policy information model defined behavior for active state and validity?

chat.author: Zhenqiang Li
chat.text: Ok. Thank you all.@Susan @Joel @Jeff

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Andrew -- the active state and validity continue to be based on fowarding plane health..

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: so if RSVP rejects a bandwidth refresh, the SID list remains active?

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: i.e RSVP control plane can control and change the SR SID list validity

chat.author: Nat Kao
chat.text:
I believe the draft is useful for operators using BGP to deploy SR-Policy CPs.
My only concern is whether "Your Discriminator" is required.
I think the headend may infer that from the CP's EP if the IGP exchanges the EP's Discriminator (RFC7883...etc).

chat.author: Nat Kao
chat.text: (to Zhenqiang Li)

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Andrew -- what you do when there is a path constraint violation is based on local policy.. -- in existing RSVP-TE deplpyments, if a bandwidth update fails, the tunnel stays UP on what was previously used..

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: and on initial turn up then?

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: on initial turn up, the TE path is typically deemed down; a local policy may define whether or not you still program the segment-list (there would be a bandwidth-reservation status that may show that signaling failed)

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: yeah so my point is the validity of a sid list will depend on whether RSVP-TE signalling succeeds, thus is a change to the validity of a SID list. Not saying it's not possible, just trying to unwind the various considerations

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Andrew -- ack

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Andrew -- Regarding the MPTE question, if we were to do the same on a Native v6 forwarding plane, it is the equivalent of programming the same IP-address route on every junction..

chat.author: liusong
chat.text: @Nat Kao Thanks for raising this. We will clarify the handling of “Your Discriminator” in a future revision of the draft.

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: @Pavan - thanks - yeah and that's where i then end up going with - is this really just Ipv6 in IPv6 tunneling with RSVP forwarding installation. i.e what does SRv6 really do for you here?

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: if i go to every node in the dag and program an ipv6 with multiple nexthops  - which maybe i use RSVP-TE to signal that instruction, what have i gained by branding it SRv6 and bringing in the SRH

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: @Andrew -- it is similar, but not quite the same; we still leverage the SRV6 service SID semantics

chat.author: Shraddha Hegde
chat.text: yes Service SID semantics comes from SRv6 so its not same as IPv6 address

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text:
thanks. 
one other Q but I decided not to ask due to time and give greg a chance: 
for the centralized locator decision making - is this only applicable when there's multi ingress? does it need to be centralized with single ingress? or can it just be locally defined blocks given to each ingress?

chat.author: Shraddha Hegde
chat.text: @Andrew The solution applies to both fully centralized or fully distributed deployment. Not sure I get your question on multi-egress

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: with a single egress, you can have the egress do this as well;  the intent is to provide a solution that caters to all options (multi-ingress/multi-egress include3d)

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text:
just to clarify - was commenting multi INgress. 
it was commented locator needs to be centralized. If there's only one INgress, does it need to be centralized ?

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: ** ( locator allocation needs to be centralized)

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: with a single ingress or egress, it need not be.

chat.author: Vishnu Beeram
chat.text: if it was a single ingress -single egress scenario, the egress can provide the same function; but the draft generalizes this..

chat.author: Andrew Stone
chat.text: ack - thanks

chat.author: Jie Dong
chat.text: draft-zzd-idr-sr-policy-scheduling is referenced in the draft, it would be good to add clarification about when CP/SID list level  is not enough?
